reviewScope: Three executable references and fifteen actual language bodies: generic circular/hash classes and oriented-piece jigsaw assembly.

questions.algorithm: Row-major backtracking over unused piece indices and all four rotations, checking perimeter and existing neighbor constraints.
questions.review: Read primary Edge/Piece/Puzzle sources and all five actual independent bodies. The callable explicitly encodes complementary edge shapes as opposite signed identifiers and returns original-input indices plus clockwise turns, without hidden original coordinates. All four perimeter iff checks reject inward flat edges; top/left joins complete every adjacency. Failed recursion clears used flags, and a completed result has one distinct pair per input piece. The general solver handles admitted impossible puzzles instead of copying the public generated-puzzle greedy assumption. C#/Java owned pair rows, Python tuples converted to lists, JS fresh pairs and C++ const input/value output are checked. Independent column-first exact-cover oracle and oriented-edge predicate execute 318 fixtures, including shuffled/rotated 2x2/3x3 assemblies, unmatched identifiers, singleton and all 2x2 input permutations. Fifteen compiled programs reject duplicate-index results and input writes while accepting reverse candidate search yielding a different valid global assembly. Correctness and conservative exponential search bounds match actual recursion.

questions.algorithm: Copy fixed storage and map logical indices through a normalized offset; each native iterator has an independent cursor.
questions.review: Read pinned Java CircularArray<T> and its test driver; the JavaScript push/pop sketch is not substituted for the iterable generic task. The independent binding starts from initial values instead of uninitialized size-only slots, with that adaptation explicit in the statement. Read all five actual class bodies. Positive rotation advances the logical front; modulo normalization occurs before bounded head addition in fixed-width languages, and empty rotation exits before division. Bounds checks precede Get/Set mapping so Python negative indexing and wrapped indices are not silently accepted. Native C#/Java generic classes, C++ template and Python Generic class preserve integer/string types; JavaScript preserves primitive types dynamically. The private harness invokes actual methods and native iteration protocols, never a user function that simulates transcript results. Independent physical list-slicing oracles cover exhaustive short operation pairs, both signed shift endpoints, invalid -1/n indices, random longer mixed traces, repeated/Unicode strings and 1000-element arrays. Separate interleaved iterators and exhaustion are exercised. Caller input storage is snapshotted throughout later updates. Twenty distinct compiled variant implementations across five languages exercise forty typed fixtures: aliasing storage, skipped negative bounds and shared cursors are rejected; inverse-offset representations remain O(1) and are accepted. The private observer never reads head/items fields or forces an offset convention. C++ value-copy Get cost and const iterator reference/proxy behavior are described accurately.

questions.algorithm: Hash into a fixed array of own linked-node chains; compare keys logically, update an existing node, prepend a new node and bypass one node on removal.
questions.review: Read pinned Java Hasher<K,V> and the linked JavaScript sketch, then all five independent actual bodies. No built-in map/dictionary/set implements table storage: C#/Java/Python use private linked Node objects, JavaScript explicit linked objects, and C++ owns raw Node chains in a vector. Hash and equality are compatible within each language, and bucket order is not a required result. C# unsigned normalization, Java floorMod, C++ size_t hash modulo, Python positive-divisor modulo and JS unsigned numeric/text hashing admit signed endpoints. Logical equality replaces the Java source identity comparison. Fresh equal-content query strings and large boxed integers make identity matching fail in compiled tests. Lookup distinguishes missing nodes from legitimate zero/empty values. Update changes Value without creating a second key node; removal preserves colliding head/interior/tail neighbors. C++ pointer-to-link removal frees the exact owned node; iterative destruction and disabled copying avoid recursive chain disposal and double ownership. Both real generic instantiations execute; the child observer calls the actual APIs, creates an independent second table and obtains final entries through Get for first-seen input keys without inspecting private fields. Trusted built-in finite-map semantics form an independent oracle across exhaustive short transcripts, deterministic collisions/updates/removals, Unicode/case distinctions, signed endpoints, random traces and 1000-node chains. Fifteen actually compiled wrong-key-match, duplicate-entry and no-op-remove variants are rejected on both generic fixtures; five tail-insertion alternatives pass. Both typed fixtures share each compiled audit program, avoiding duplicate builds. Fixed capacity and hash/equality/copy costs are included in the stated expected/worst complexity rather than claiming unconditional constant lookup.

Get/Set/Rotate delegates enforce the declared generic result and void methods. Both integer and string instantiations compile and execute. HashTable<K,V> constrains nonnull keys and uses EqualityComparer<K>.Default. Node keys are readonly, values update in place, bucket indices normalize the full signed hash through uint, and typed Action/Func bindings verify the API. Strings are queried through fresh equal-content copies. Jigsaw reads pieces through rotated-side indices without changing input rows, uses owned placement/used arrays, and returns a concrete row-major pair list after complete backtracking success.
